rubric_notes: Complete. Verified a.22 single superfamily, a.22.1 families with sunids and member proteins, d1r4va_. Correctly ranks relationship by level (family < superfamily < fold/class), states superfamily implies probable homology but not shared function, keeps domain-level scope for TAF4/Sos/macroH2A, and notes fold-sharing alone is insufficient. Linker histone a.4.5 lineage stated transparently as background knowledge (correct) and phrased as SCOPe not relating them. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Lineages, sunids, boundaries and annotations supported by bundle (release 2.08 visible in node records). Remote homology at superfamily level with correct contrast to fold-only similarity. Rejects transfer in both directions, frames shared active-site architecture as hypothesis to test, dismisses Li/UNL, notes boundary difference, lists required external evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct families c.55.1.1/.3/.4 with sunids under c.55.1 (53067), fold c.55, class c, release 2.08, all supported by the evidence bundle including the duplication comment. Infers remote common ancestry and a conserved two-lobe ATP-binding core; explicitly refuses to transfer substrate, chemistry, regulation, partner binding, polymer formation, or cellular role. Distinguishes fold-level neighbours (c.55.3 etc.) from superfamily homology without asserting non-homology. No material issues. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Hierarchy, sunids, comments, members, Pfam supported. Superfamily = probable homology via conserved dimetal site, fold alone insufficient, chemistry divergence in metal/substrate/oligomer, explicit unsafe transfers, requires HMM, structural alignment of ligands and experimental metal/activity data; notes curated not proven. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Correct b.6.1.1/b.6.1.5/b.6.1.6 in b.6.1 with sunids, lineage, Pfam mappings and curator comments all supported by bundle. Superfamily interpreted as probable distant common ancestry, stronger than fold but weaker than family; copper binding and electron transfer explicitly withheld from ephrin and PAD4 with SCOPe's annotations cited; required evidence (conserved His/Cys/His/Met ligands, metal-bound structure, spectroscopy, assays) listed. Background note that PAD4 catalytic domain is a different SCOPe fold is correct. No material issues.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Hierarchy and sunids correct; the claim that d1ubqa_ and d1rfaa_ share superfamily as lowest common node and carry no annotation or homology caveats is supported by the parents, annotations and homology endpoints in the bundle. Correct remote-homology interpretation, fold-level caveat, and explicit rejection of transferring conjugation, p97 binding and Ras binding; lists family-level evidence needed and cautions against automated matches as curated evidence.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Correct families, sunids, superfamily, fold and class; Pfam and KaiA annotations supported. Superfamily-level distant common ancestry distinguished from fold sharing and from family-level closeness. Rejects receiver chemistry transfer, KaiA phospho-relay inference, ODC wing catalysis/PLP, reverse transfer of catalysis, and template/representative misuse; notes PLP catalysis sits in separately classified c.67.1 domains (domain recruitment). External evidence requirements stated.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Hierarchy, sunids, species for both protein entries and PubMed citation supported by bundle. Correctly frames strong claim (V1/A1 homologous at family/superfamily level) versus weak claim (shared fold b.84, not homology; convergence or undetectable ancestry both possible). Rejects function transfer, template use and pooling in representative sets; notes sparse population. Background (NHR absent in F-type) flagged. Concise but complete.

Fold, sunids, three superfamilies, and fold comment supported by bundle. Correctly separates fold-level architecture from superfamily homology, treats convergence as a possibility and homology as a hypothesis needing extra evidence, rejects function/template/benchmark pooling, and names sequence, profile, structural-detail, and functional/genomic-context evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct hierarchy, sunids, family comment, PF02254 and sibling families, all supported ('about ten other families' is accurate). Fold could be convergent; superfamily carries the evolutionary claim; separate families = no close sequence relationship and divergent roles (ADH cofactor domain with b.35.1 partner, CoA binding, non-catalytic RCK gating). Bars transfer of catalytic residues, reaction, substrate, NAD/NADP/CoA preference and gating; treats shared ligand class as a hypothesis; multidomain caveat; names required external evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage, identifiers and lowest shared node (family k.40.1.1); correct conclusion that the generic homology flag should not be read as proof. States 'no caveat annotations' because only domain-level annotations were checked; the family-node 'not a true family' comment (must_include 2/3) is never retrieved or mentioned. Transfer limits and external-evidence needs are appropriate.

All must_include met with bundle-supported identifiers: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 (own fold/superfamily) vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 with class as lowest shared node; 2.08 d1t1ja1 (1-118) c.23.14.2 and d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 with superfamily c.23.14 as lowest shared node. Complete: synthetic N-terminal tag in class l l.1.1.1 for H:1-8, d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 with Fab NC10 comment, l-class levels as bookkeeping, tag similarity rejected, no transfer of labels in either direction, fold-vs-superfamily strength noted. Correct 1.75 whole-chain d1acca_ (43828, f.11.1.1) in a self-referential lineage, unchanged in 2.03, split from 2.04 and unchanged through 2.08 into d1acca2 (238522, A:14-225, b.179.1.1) and d1acca1 (238521, A:226-735, f.60.1.1). Treats the PA14-like superfamily's GLEYA, GH31 and automated-match families as evidence that the N-terminal unit is an independently recombined module, grades family, superfamily and fold evidence correctly, notes the new fold was created alongside the superfamily, and blocks toxin and carbohydrate-binding transfer. Separates API-derived facts from background knowledge and discloses which releases were not checked.

All must_include met; identifiers, boundaries, sccs and Pfam PF12134 mapping for family 159638 are bundle-supported. Good interpretation of reuse vs innovation, superfamily-level homology, no function transfer, Jab1/MPN coverage gap. Factual slip: asserts each domain sits in a different class, fold and superfamily, but a1 and a2 are both class c. Noncentral. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14.

Complete: correct lineage, protein and species nodes, ATOM-based lengths consistent with the retrieved sequences, the 'single repeat' comment, the 're' inconsistency code with its meaning, and the family repeat unit 4cj9 A:259-292 applying only to d4cj9a_. Explicitly states that length and repeat count are not evidence for or against family membership, that shared fold alone would not establish homology while the family assignment does, and that comparisons must be made repeat-to-repeat. Rejects DNA-specificity transfer across PthA/dHax3/BurrH and flags the NMR fragment as a poor whole-array template and the uncovered N/C-terminal regions. Evaluator: Claude SCOPe benchmark grader, 2026-10-14.

Correct, supported metadata including api path and periodic 2.08-2026-08-16. Cites stable 2.08 pinned in calls, rejects 'current', preserves exact dated identifier plus access date when periodic-only content is used. Periodic semantics: dated content snapshot within the 2.08 series, not a new major release, adds newly deposited PDB structures mostly by automated classification while 2.08-stable remains fixed and curated. Appropriate caveats on automated assignments and is_comprehensive. Complete.

All must_include items present and bundle-supported: shared a.47.2.1 lineage; fragment comment and 'ms' flag on d1br0a_/d1ez3a_; fold definition of four long helices used to show the three-helix fragments resemble a spectrin repeat and inherit the fold from the complete domain; 1dn1 B supplies the complete closed conformation, is obsolete (3c98) and an automated match to d3c98b_. Correctly distinguishes family/superfamily homology from fold-level similarity, rejects spectrin homology without asserting non-homology, rejects function/conformation transfer, and advises treating fragment folds as provisional until a complete domain supports them. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Clear convergence vs divergence treatment (c.2.1 divergent; c.3/c.4 kept separate as unproven; c.1.7 TIM barrel as convergent recruitment), domain-by-domain analysis of multi-domain dehydrogenases (b.35.1, d.81.1, c.23.12), and explicit SCOP evidence ranking by level. Evidence integration covers HMM-HMM, structural superposition with statistics, unusual topology, binding mode, non-functional conserved residues, domain context. Closes with 'separate folds = ancestry not established, neither proof of independent origin nor homology'. All sunids supported by bundle; c.25.1 and family names correctly flagged as from knowledge. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Accurate throughout: 2.04 shared nothing below class b, with ColG in b.23.2 under CUB-like b.23 and Cry3A domain III in b.18.1.3 under b.18.1; current 2.08 has ColG in new family b.18.1.36 (sunid 267607) inside b.18.1 with SIDs and sunids retained, the short chain B segment split into l.1.1.1, and Cry3A unchanged, so the lowest shared node moved from class to superfamily while families remain separate. Reclassification correctly dated to 2.05 from the per-release lookups, and the other Cry3A domains are excluded from the relationship. Cites the retrieved family comment and explains the link to Cry3A is indirect via the Cry4Ba domain in the same family. Explicitly states the shared fold is not what establishes homology, that sequence evidence was not examined and is expected to be negligible, and that ligand, Ca-site, specificity and template transfer are not licensed; also recommends release-specific citation. The background-knowledge resolution figure for 1nqd is unverified but immaterial. Evaluator: Claude, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage with sunids, boundaries, comments, non-inherited hf and homology flags; correctly notes shared node is below family. Quality values cited are correct release values though not in this bundle. Reasoning complete: homology at protein level; hf as mutation-induced conformational state, not separate lineage; rejects template use both ways, training mislabeling, representative choice and native DNA-recognition geometry transfer; notes hf flag does not quantify deviation and lists needed structural evidence.

Lineage, sunids, fr/cr9 annotations, SEQRES/ATOM counts correct. Did not retrieve SPACI/AEROSPACI or method for either entry (acknowledged), so representative recommendation lacks quality fields. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. All must_include met: new superfamily in existing fold with new family; family in existing superfamily is the strongest claim and asserts probable common ancestry; new fold is a structural claim requiring different core topology and is not justified by missing ancestry evidence; placement is a provisional, revisable, release-specific hypothesis. Rejects function/template transfer across superfamilies. d.58 example supported by bundle, correctly noting more children beyond the first page.

Families, sunids and superfamily correctly stated and supported by the bundle. Clear statement that the relationship is superfamily-level not family-level, that superfamily asserts probable common ancestry beyond fold, and that substrate class and canonical-kinase regulation cannot be transferred. Evidence requirements include family-level placement via profile hits, residue-level catalytic and substrate-site checks, domain architecture, template quality (SPACI used correctly as a structure-quality metric), and experimental confirmation.
